changelog: 1.0.0-beta.11: Home header artwork restored to the look that rendered correctly. Hero cards carry the portrait Kitsu poster as their image and no longer send a `backdrop`: the app paints `backdrop` across the full-screen header, so the 4:1 Kitsu cover was being crop-filled into a narrow, zoomed slice (only the rare 16:9 cover survived). Detail pages use the same poster and also stop sending `backdrop`. Titles, search and players are unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.10: Home hero cards use the wide Kitsu cover artwork again (the original header look), while grid cards and detail pages keep the full portrait poster. Titles, search and players are unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.9: Hero cards and detail pages go back to the original portrait poster artwork. The 2.7-4.2:1 Kitsu cover had been used as the main image, so the app crop-filled it into a narrow slice and the header looked massively zoomed; the wide cover is now only exposed as banner/backdrop. This also stops the detail page from showing a cropped banner instead of the whole poster.

1.0.0-beta.8: Search now answers in about 1-2 s (streaming worker pool that starts on the first source, a 2.6 s verification budget, negative caching of franime misses and a 3-minute query cache). Titles are always English or French, never romaji or Japanese (Blue Box stays Blue Box, The Apothecary Diaries keeps its French subtitle). Home rows use the 550x780 Kitsu posters. vidmoly is the default player when available, then sibnet, and every verified player is listed in the Quality picker.

1.0.0-beta.7: Hero cards now use the 1981-2048 px Kitsu banner artwork instead of the small portrait poster, and text search is rebuilt around French titles (AniList search mapped to Kitsu, in parallel with Kitsu text search, 8.5 s deadline, bounded verification, Kitsu-card fallback): a French query now answers in about 2 s instead of failing after a delay.

1.0.0-beta.6: High-resolution posters (original Kitsu artwork instead of the 284x402 thumbnails), a square 512x512 header icon, and search reworked to finish inside the app budget (9 s deadline, 4-way franime verification, Kitsu-card fallback when franime is rate-limited) so it no longer fails after a delay.
1.0.0-beta.5: Private repository identity SP-VID-9001-FRANIME allocated. No playback code change; the package was rebuilt so the repository index has unique module identities.

1.0.0-beta.5: Signed HLS masters carried by the catalogue are played directly, quality labels are normalised to standard tiers (1076p becomes 1080p) and deduplicated, and a title whose upload only offers 360p now lists every available quality with an explicit notice instead of silently capping playback. The maximum quality still depends on the uploaded file.

1.0.0-beta.4: Quality picker now lists every HLS rendition exposed by the uqload source, highest first, plus an adaptive Auto option; numeric title suffixes no longer trigger a false source-mismatch block. The maximum quality still depends on the uploaded file.
1.0.0-beta.3: Private repository identity SP-VID-9002-NOVA-STREAM allocated. No playback code change; the package was rebuilt so the repository index has unique module identities.
1.0.0-beta.2: Previous NOVA package (public catalogue with films, series, search, details, episodes and VF playback through public uqload embeds).

1.0.0-beta.6: Highest checked quality is now the default. Vidzy's own files cap at 480p (its master carries a single 864x488 rendition), while the moviez source of the same catalogue exposes 1080p and 720p for many titles, so the picker was opening the 480p file while taller renditions sat unused. Every checked rendition from every reader is now listed highest first and the tallest one opens: L'Odyssee, Masterplan and Fall 2 start at Moviez 1080p, Vidzy 480p and Moviez 720p remain selectable, and a title where only Vidzy exists (Outer Banks S01E01/E02) still plays. Each entry keeps its player name and quality. The Vidzy Firefox-UA fix from beta.5 is unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.5: Outer Banks S01E01/E02 and every title that only exposes Vidzy now start. The Vidzy CDN answers a 176-byte self-looping decoy to Chrome/Edge fingerprints whose Accept-Encoding lacks br+zstd, which is what most player stacks send, and hard-blocks ExoPlayer/VLC/ffmpeg user agents, so the old headers left those episodes spinning on "starting the video player" forever while titles with an HD/Moviez fallback recovered. Vidzy requests now use a Firefox user agent with identity encoding: the CDN returns the real 488-byte master and its 330-segment media playlist whatever the player sends. The ladder is verified before returning; HD and Moviez fallbacks are unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.4: Vidzy is now the default player and always appears first. Its CDN filters non-browser clients, so the module no longer discards it when its own probe receives the 177-byte decoy: the signed HLS master is handed to the app's player, which uses the device network stack, and is parsed into a real ladder when the probe does return it. Every picker entry now carries its player name (Vidzy, HD, Moviez) because the app relabels height-bearing entries, and HD/Moviez stay as labelled fallbacks where they offer a taller rendition.

1.0.0-beta.3: Player and quality in one picker. Vidzy (the site's first player) is now the default reader: its page, embed, HLS key and playlist are resolved first, and it is only offered when its media playlist and first segment answer as real media. The HD reader and the moviez source are resolved in parallel and their renditions appear in the same Quality list (for example "Moviez VOSTFR · 1080p"), so the viewer switches player and quality from one menu.

1.0.0-beta.2: Playback now starts on the titles the HD reader does not index. The resolver reads the reader session id from its own script, tries every announced source in availability order (including the one it first flags unverified), waits out the warming answer instead of mistaking it for a failure, follows the HLS proxy player used by recent releases, and stops rejecting playable playlists because of a host-name check. When the HD reader has no usable lane, the moviez source of the same catalogue takes over in VF (VOSTFR when VF is missing). Popular titles that used to end on "le lecteur HD n a pas fourni de flux lisible" now play.

1.0.0-beta.1: New CineRegal module (cineregal.onl): French TMDB catalogue with multi search, details, seasons/episodes and discovery (trending, popular, top rated). Playback goes through the site's public HD reader (fluxora.sbs): the signed HLS gateway is resolved from the embed page, validated, and every available rendition is exposed highest first. Titles without an available source fail with an explicit message.

1.0.0-beta.3: The site now answers every playback request (movies and episodes alike) with HTTP 403 and {"error":"Verification anti-robot requise pour lancer la lecture.","code":"human_required"}: it requires a browser anti-bot challenge before it releases a file. That challenge cannot be satisfied by a module and this one does not try to; instead of the old bare "HTTP 403" the player now receives an explicit message saying the site asks for an anti-robot check in a browser, so the real cause is visible. Catalogue, search, details and episode lists are unaffected (episode-videos still answers HTTP 200 and keeps its video-url playback). Playback stays unavailable until the site removes that gate.

1.0.0-beta.2: Episodes now carry the intro and outro skip markers the site's own player shows. The series' IMDb id is resolved through the site's TMDB proxy, the public IntroDB endpoint the site proxies is queried for the episode, and the segments are converted to seconds and validated (end after start) before being attached as intro/outro, the skip metadata of contract v4. The lookups run in parallel with the video resolution and are cached in memory (IMDb id 7 days, segments 30 min), so start-up time is unchanged. When IntroDB has no data for an episode the fields are simply absent and playback is untouched; movies never carry them. Recap and post-credits markers stay out because the contract has no field for them.

1.0.0-beta.1: New StreamFlix module (stream-flix.lol): French VF catalogue of 8,000+ movies and 850+ series with search, details, seasons/episodes and discovery (a la une, latest additions, best rated). Search hits the site index first and, when an unaccented query returns nothing ("odyssee" vs "L'Odyssee"), falls back to TMDB multi-search filtered through the catalogue lookup so only playable titles appear. Playback goes through the public video-url API: the CDN answers two 302 hops (proxy, then a signed ?ff= MP4 link), and the module resolves both with Range probes and hands the player and the downloader the signed file with the exact headers, instead of a routing URL that loses headers on redirect. Files are progressive MP4 (streamType mp4, downloadable); measured renditions include The Odyssey 1920x1080, Outer Banks S1 1920x960, The Rookie S1 1080p and S8 720p, Dune Prophecy 1920x960. The site's own quality field (HD) is what the picker reports. Titles or episodes without a file fail with an explicit message.

1.0.0-beta.5: Fiches now carry the current season's poster, the way the site's own catalogue does. Les Carnets de l'Apothicaire showed its season 1 artwork while the home header already used season 3; the fiche now uses season 3 (the wheat-field artwork). Bleach uses its latest cour poster and The Ramparts of Ice its largest one. A poster below the 1920 size threshold is skipped for the newest one that clears it, so a fiche never drops to a 700 px image. The home header is curated: Bleach and The Ramparts of Ice open the rotation and Bocchi the Rock! and Journal with Witch are excluded. Episode lists, playback and discovery rows are unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.4: Titles that exposed no episode now list everything the catalogue actually publishes. Films (5 Centimeters per Second and every other film of a series) appear as entries named after the film and open their own film page: the detail page names the films, the film page carries one reader per film in release order, and playback picks the same index in VOSTFR or VF. Airing seasons (Les Carnets de l'Apothicaire S3, Blue Box S2, The Detective Is Already Dead S2) have no declared episode count on the site, so the module now reads the same public episode feed the site's own player uses and lists the episodes already released (measured: Apothecary 54 episodes over 3 seasons, Blue Box 30 over 2, Detective 17 over 2, HLS 1080p on the new episodes). A released season whose detail page omits a count is recovered the same way instead of showing nothing, and the fiche's episode total now counts the airing episodes (48 became 54) instead of advertising the stale figure. Titles without any playable source still fail with the explicit message from beta.1.

1.0.0-beta.3: The home header no longer receives a wide `backdrop` from details. The app paints that field full-screen and crop-filled the 16:9 affiche down to a narrow slice, so the header still looked massively zoomed even after hero cards switched to portrait posters. Detail pages now expose the portrait season poster as image/poster at the 1920 variant and keep the wide affiche only as `banner`, which is the combination the other French modules render correctly. Detail pages also probe the first and last season posters of a title (up to six HEAD requests, about 300 ms in parallel with the page read) and keep the heaviest one, so a title whose season 1 poster is only 736 px wide (One Piece) is served its 1920 px current-season poster instead. Playback is unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.2: The home header now rotates through the best-rated catalogue instead of always replaying the site's static premiere (JoJo's Bizarre Adventure), presenting six titles at a time and excluding the static premiere. Hero artwork switches from the 16:9 key art to the portrait season poster at its largest variant and no longer sends `backdrop`, so the app's tall header no longer crop-fills a narrow slice of a landscape image. Source posters range from 300x400 to 1920x2880 with no dimensions exposed, so the module HEAD-checks the 1920 variant of each candidate and keeps only files of 160 KB or more (about 1200 px wide and above, measured 1200x1600 to 1920x2880; the 300-750 px posters weigh 16-90 KB) before choosing the six. The header shows exactly the artwork that was checked, never a smaller season image from the detail page. Hero cards also carry genres, themes, status, season and episode counts. Playback code is unchanged.

1.0.0-beta.1: New Mugiwara module (mugiwara-no-streaming.com): public French anime catalogue in VOSTFR and VF with search, details, seasons/episodes and discovery (a la une, best rated, Action, A-Z catalogue). Playback reads the public ansembed/voembed embed of the selected episode, extracts the signed HLS master and lists the renditions actually present (1080p and 480p measured on checked titles), highest first. Audio keys are matched by language (vf, vf1/vf2, named VF rows) and the requested language is never silently swapped for the other one; a title or an episode without a reader fails with an explicit message. Side seasons (hs/oav), films and season-less one-shots stay out.
